task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after form-submit routing, gate checks and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or fetch call.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from adjusted character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The fetch URL and X-Query-Pack header name are assembled from character-code arrays, obscuring the network request destination.
The target query_pack value is carried through a state-machine transit and a runtime-selected reducer slot before console output and fetch header assignment.
The filter route selects its active reducer slot only after form-submit-time scope, term and depth state are captured.
The reducer table contains 32 entries; only slot 23 is selected by the live filter path.

The form-submit path crosses delegated submit handling, command routing, lane gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local CustomEvent dispatch, an eight-layer middleware chain, a state-machine trampoline, reducer selection, query_pack construction, fetch header assignment and sink wrapping.
The deployed bundle contains 44 decoy x-modules and 25 vendor-noise v-modules that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target query_pack field.
The reducer table exposes 31 inactive reducer closures whose bodies are structurally identical to the live slot-23 reducer, making visual identification without tracing the slot selection impossible.
The target value is separated from the submit click by queueMicrotask, Promise.resolve, setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The state-machine trampoline runs 3104 steps to derive the transit state passed to the reducer; the transit value changes the reducer branch and output.
The fetch call site and console.log sink both receive an already-constructed query_pack value, so sink or network inspection alone does not identify the construction site.
The active reducer is stored in a Map and retrieved via the slot id provided by o2() at runtime, making static analysis of which reducer runs non-trivial.

behavior_category.subtype: form-submit-time filter fields packed value written to request header
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic pack of filter scope, search term and depth fields reduced through a slot-selected state-machine reducer, written to the X-Query-Pack header of a fetch POST request. It is not a state-only code, browser fingerprint or static signature.

near_categories.why_not: The output is not console-only; the same value is also assigned to a fetch request header field, making this a request transformation case.
The output has no cryptographic proof or seal semantics; the reducer produces a compact deterministic value from form state, not an HMAC or asymmetric proof.
The chain uses local DOM form state and runtime slot selection, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
